shortcut_name: connected n-vertex graph with n-1 edges is a tree
evidence: deepseek: "Root at any vertex in T"; gpt-oss: "root the tree at 1"; glm: constructs parent arrays after reading the graph
affordance_in_statement: You are given that m = n - 1. Furthermore, it is mathematically guaranteed that if you were to select all m available 1-simplices, the resulting complex would have dim H_0(X; R) = 1
secondary_shortcut_name: reduce rank-one inclusion to connecting all critical vertices
removal_suggestion: There is no semantics-preserving rewording that removes this tree structure: the fixed edge count together with the connectedness guarantee forces a tree. To defeat the shortcut, the scenario must instead permit non-tree catalogs, for example by no longer guaranteeing that all available 1-simplices form a connected complex.

common_affordance: The available 1-simplices form a connected graph on n vertices with exactly n-1 edges, so the catalog is necessarily a tree

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: Uses a generic Kruskal/MST-style approach rather than exploiting the required minimum subtree connecting only the vertices in T; it does not correctly solve the tree-Steiner-subtree objective.

recommended_edit: Replace the guarantee that selecting all m available 1-simplices produces a connected complex with a promise that the catalog may contain disconnected components and cycles, while retaining the examples as valid instances. This removes the universal tree reduction and forces solutions to handle the general connectivity structure.
regression_risk: The edit changes the underlying problem from a tree problem to a substantially harder general graph problem; it may also invalidate assumptions in already-defeated MST-based solutions in unpredictable ways.
